title: Fetal growth and fetal movements
blurb: Measure and plot fundal height to Saving Babies' Lives v3, and manage reduced fetal movements with the ask, act, advise checklist.
question: Amara, 34+2 weeks in her first pregnancy, phones the maternity triage line at 23:00. Her baby has moved less than usual since the afternoon. Her last fundal height, 2 weeks ago, was on the 50th centile. What should the midwife advise, and what assessment follows?

teach.h: Two windows on the baby's wellbeing
teach.body: Formally: Saving Babies' Lives Care Bundle v3 (SBL v3) element 2 covers fetal growth (risk assessment, surveillance and management of fetal growth restriction, FGR) and element 3 covers raising awareness of reduced fetal movements (RFM). In plain English: a growing baby who moves in its usual pattern is reassuring. A baby who is falling off its growth curve, or moving less, may have a struggling placenta, and the midwife must act the same day.
teach.cite: NHS England SBL v3.2 elements 2 and 3; NICE NG201 1.2.29–1.2.35

items.label: FGR risk assessment
items.sub: booking; reviewed again in the second trimester

items.label: Uterine artery Doppler
items.sub: women at high risk of FGR

items.label: SFH starts; discuss movements
items.sub: ask about movements at every contact

items.sub: then movements discussed at every contact

items.sub: then no more often than every 2 weeks

values: Uterine artery Doppler if high risk

teach.caption: Do not routinely offer scans after 28 weeks for uncomplicated singleton pregnancies (NG201 1.2.33).

children.label: Offer a growth and wellbeing scan
children.sub: urgency guided by RFM or raised BP

teach.caption: NICE NG201 1.2.31–1.2.32; staff measuring SFH must be trained to measure, plot and refer (SBL v3 2.11).

teach.body: There is no set number of kicks a baby should make. A woman should get to know her own baby's usual pattern and contact maternity services straight away, day or night, if movements reduce, stop or change. She should not wait until the next day, count kicks for hours, or use a home Doppler: hearing a heartbeat does not mean the baby is well. Movements continue right up to and during labour.

steps.sub: review chart, SFH if none in 2 weeks, cCTG

steps.sub: share results; reattend with any concern

teach.caption: If the fetal heart cannot be heard, arrange an immediate ultrasound assessment.

teach.h: Scenario: Amara on the triage line
teach.body: The midwife tells Amara to come in now, not to wait until morning. On arrival the midwife asks the checklist questions, auscultates the fetal heart, reviews her growth chart and measures SFH (none in the last 2 weeks), then performs a computerised CTG. Both are normal and this is her first episode, so no scan is needed. The midwife explains the results, documents them and asks Amara to call again at any time if movements reduce.

teach.text: Do not advise kick counting, a cold drink and a lie-down, or a home Doppler before calling. And once a woman starts serial growth scans, STOP plotting SFH: the scans replace it (SBL v3 2.12).

items: FGR risk assessment by 14 weeks; high risk: uterine artery Doppler 18+0 to 23+6, then scans every 3 to 4 weeks.
Low risk: SFH from 24+0, first by 28+6, no more often than every 2 weeks, plotted on a chart.
Small SFH: offer a scan; large SFH: consider a scan.
RFM: attend straight away; ask, act (heartbeat, growth, cCTG), advise.
Recurrent RFM after 28+0: scan growth, liquor and Doppler unless scanned in the last 2 weeks.
After 38+6 discuss induction; not for RFM alone before 39+0.

summary: You can now place fundal height and growth scans on the right pathway and act on a small or large measurement. You can also respond to reduced fetal movements using the SBL v3 ask, act, advise checklist, including when a scan or birth should be offered.

A.q: For a woman at low risk of fetal growth restriction, by what gestation should the first symphysis fundal height measurement be completed under SBL v3?
options: By 24+0 weeks
By 28+6 weeks
By 32+0 weeks
By 20+6 weeks
A.why: SBL v3 2.10: serial SFH at each appointment after 24+0 weeks, with the first measurement carried out by 28+6 weeks.

whyNot.0: 24+0 is when SFH measurement starts, not the deadline for the first one.
whyNot.2: 32+0 is later than the SBL v3 deadline of 28+6.
whyNot.3: SFH is not started before 24+0 weeks.

A.q: Jo, 30 weeks pregnant, phones at 22:00. Her baby has moved less than usual since the afternoon. What is the most appropriate advice from the midwife?
options: Count kicks for two hours and ring back
Attend the antenatal clinic in the morning
Come in now to be assessed
Listen with a home Doppler and ring back
A.why: Women should contact maternity services and be assessed straight away, day or night, when movements reduce (NG201 1.2.34; SBL v3 element 3).

whyNot.0: There is no set number of movements and kick counting delays assessment.
whyNot.1: Waiting until the next day delays assessment of a possibly compromised baby.
whyNot.3: Home Dopplers are unreliable; hearing a heartbeat does not mean the baby is well.

A.q: Priya is at increased risk of FGR and starts serial growth scans at 28 weeks. What should happen to her symphysis fundal height measurements?
options: Stop them once serial scans begin
Continue them every 2 weeks as well
Measure weekly between the scans
Measure at each scan appointment
A.why: SBL v3 2.12: women having planned serial scan surveillance should stop SFH measurement once scans begin.

whyNot.1: Duplicating SFH alongside scans is not recommended once scan surveillance starts.
whyNot.2: SFH is not measured more often than every 2 weeks, and stops on a scan pathway.
whyNot.3: The scan itself gives the growth estimate; SFH is not repeated alongside it.

B.q: Grace, 32 weeks, attends with reduced movements for the second time in 10 days. Her cCTG is normal and her last growth scan was 5 weeks ago. What should be offered?
options: Scan growth, liquor and umbilical artery Doppler
Reassurance and discharge home without a further scan
Induction of labour within the next week
A daily kick chart for the next seven days
B.why: Recurrent RFM after 28+0 weeks: offer an ultrasound scan for growth, liquor volume and umbilical artery Doppler, unless a scan was done in the previous 2 weeks (SBL v3 element 3).

whyNot.1: A normal cCTG is not enough with recurrent RFM; a scan is indicated.
whyNot.2: Induction for RFM alone is not recommended before 39+0 weeks.
whyNot.3: Kick charts are not recommended; there is no set number of movements.

B.q: At 30 weeks, Ruth's fundal height plots below the expected curve and her blood pressure is newly raised. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Repeat the SFH measurement in 2 weeks
Offer a growth and wellbeing scan
Ask another midwife to remeasure next week
Arrange a scan at the 36-week appointment
B.why: A small-for-dates SFH needs an ultrasound scan for fetal growth and wellbeing, with urgency guided by findings such as raised blood pressure or RFM (NG201 1.2.32).

whyNot.0: Waiting 2 weeks delays assessment of a possibly growth-restricted baby.
whyNot.2: Remeasuring next week delays the scan that NG201 says to offer.
whyNot.3: Six weeks' delay is unsafe with a small SFH and raised BP.

B.q: Sana, 39+1 weeks, reports a single episode of reduced movements. Her CTG and growth are normal. What does SBL v3 advise the midwife to do?
options: Discuss induction of labour with her
Offer a planned caesarean birth
Book a repeat scan in 2 weeks
Arrange a membrane sweep at 41 weeks
B.why: For any RFM after 38+6 weeks, discuss induction of labour with the woman (risks, benefits and her wishes), using the patient decision aid.

whyNot.1: Caesarean birth is not offered for RFM in an otherwise normal pregnancy.
whyNot.2: A delayed scan does not address the advice to discuss birth after 38+6.
whyNot.3: Deferring to 41 weeks ignores the SBL v3 advice for RFM after 38+6 weeks.

C.q: Leah, 36+0 weeks, attends triage with reduced movements. The midwife cannot find the fetal heart with a hand-held Doppler after repositioning. What is the next step?
options: Start a CTG and review in 20 minutes
Arrange an immediate ultrasound assessment
Try a Pinard and recheck in an hour
Book a growth scan for the next working day
C.why: SBL v3 RFM checklist: if the fetal heart cannot be auscultated with a hand-held Doppler or Pinard, arrange an immediate ultrasound assessment of viability.

whyNot.0: A CTG may record the maternal pulse; viability must be confirmed by ultrasound now.
whyNot.2: Waiting an hour delays confirming viability.
whyNot.3: A next-day growth scan does not answer whether the baby is alive now.

C.q: Mei, 34 weeks, has a second episode of reduced movements in a week. Her growth scan 10 days ago was normal, and today's cCTG and SFH are normal. What is the most appropriate plan?
options: Repeat the growth scan before she goes home today
Offer induction of labour later this week
Admit her for daily CTG until the birth
No scan; advise her to reattend if worried
C.why: A scan is not required if a normal growth scan was done in the previous 2 weeks. Share the results and encourage her to reattend with any further concern (SBL v3 element 3).

whyNot.0: A repeat scan is not needed within 2 weeks of a normal growth scan.
whyNot.1: Induction for RFM alone is not recommended before 39+0 weeks.
whyNot.2: Daily CTG admission is not part of the SBL v3 pathway with normal findings.

C.q: At booking, Hannah is assessed as high risk of FGR. Besides serial growth scans, which test does SBL v3 recommend for her?
options: Weekly CTG monitoring from 24 weeks onwards
Twice-weekly SFH measurement from 24 weeks
Planned induction of labour at 37+0 weeks
Uterine artery Doppler at 18+0 to 23+6
C.why: SBL v3 2.7: women at high risk of FGR should have uterine artery Doppler assessment between 18+0 and 23+6 weeks.

whyNot.0: Routine weekly CTG is not part of the FGR pathway.
whyNot.1: SFH is not measured more often than every 2 weeks, and stops on a scan pathway.
whyNot.2: Timing of birth depends on scan findings, not on risk status at booking.

reteach.title: The tape and the kicks
reteach.question: Think of two simple signals: a tape measure on the bump, and the woman's sense of her baby's pattern. What does each tell the midwife, and what does she do when one changes?

blocks.body: Both signals reflect how well the placenta is feeding the baby. The tape (SFH) is measured at each antenatal appointment after 24 weeks, no more often than every 2 weeks, and plotted on a chart; a curve that flattens or a point below the line means a scan. The kicks are monitored by the woman herself every day; a change in her baby's usual pattern means a same-day assessment.

blocks.text: Counting a set number of kicks is not the advice. The woman's own baby's usual pattern is the benchmark.

explain.body: Measure SFH at each appointment after 24+0 weeks, no more often than every 2 weeks, with the first by 28+6. Plot it on a growth chart. Small: offer a scan. Large: consider a scan.

test.q: How often should symphysis fundal height be measured in a low-risk pregnancy after 24 weeks?
options: Every week from 24 weeks until the birth
At each visit, at most every 2 weeks
Every 4 weeks, starting from 28 weeks
At every contact, starting from 20 weeks
test.why: NG201 1.2.30 and SBL v3 2.10: at each antenatal appointment after 24+0 weeks, but no more frequently than every 2 weeks.

whyNot.0: Weekly is more often than recommended.
whyNot.2: SFH starts at 24+0 and is measured at each appointment, not 4-weekly from 28.
whyNot.3: SFH is not started before 24+0 weeks.

explain.body: Ask about the episode. Act: listen to the fetal heart to confirm viability, review growth and measure SFH if not done in 2 weeks, and perform a CTG (ideally computerised). Advise: explain results and encourage reattendance.

test.q: A woman attends with reduced movements at 31 weeks. What is the midwife's first clinical action after taking the history?
options: Book a growth scan for the following morning
Ask her to lie on her side and count movements
Auscultate the fetal heart to confirm viability
Give a cold drink and recheck movements in an hour
test.why: The SBL v3 checklist starts the 'act' stage by auscultating the fetal heart (hand-held Doppler or Pinard) to confirm viability.

whyNot.0: A scan may follow, but viability is confirmed first, today.
whyNot.1: Counting movements delays assessment and is not part of the checklist.
whyNot.3: Drinks and waiting are not part of the checklist and delay assessment.

explain.body: First episode with a normal cCTG and no other indication: no scan. Recurrent RFM after 28+0: offer a scan of growth, liquor volume and umbilical artery Doppler, unless a normal scan was done in the previous 2 weeks.

test.q: Which assessments make up the scan offered for recurrent reduced movements after 28 weeks?
options: Placental site, cervical length and fetal growth
Nuchal translucency, liquor volume and placental site
Biophysical profile and cervical length measurement
Growth, liquor volume and umbilical artery Doppler
test.why: SBL v3 element 3: ultrasound for fetal growth, liquor volume and umbilical artery Doppler.

whyNot.0: Cervical length assesses preterm birth risk, not placental function.
whyNot.1: Nuchal translucency is a first-trimester screening measurement.
whyNot.2: This combination is not the SBL v3 RFM scan.

explain.body: After 38+6 weeks, discuss induction with every woman who reports RFM and offer birth to those with recurrent RFM. Before 39+0 weeks, induction for RFM alone is not recommended without evidence of compromise or other concerns.

test.q: At 37+2 weeks, Ella has had one episode of reduced movements with normal cCTG and growth. She asks for an induction. What does SBL v3 say?
options: Offer induction of labour within the next 24 hours
Offer induction after any second episode of RFM
Induction for RFM alone is not recommended yet
Offer a planned caesarean birth at 38 weeks
test.why: SBL v3: induction of labour before 39 weeks is recommended only with evidence of fetal compromise or other concerns in addition to RFM.

whyNot.0: With normal findings there is no indication for induction before 39 weeks.
whyNot.1: A second episode leads to a scan before 38+6, not automatic induction.
whyNot.3: Caesarean birth is not indicated for RFM with normal findings.
